subject: Finish-line checklist: evaluation verification & exit tests
messages:
From: Alyssa Green <alyssa@clipperhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: QA Team <qa@clipperhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T15:12:00Z
Subject: Finish-line checklist: evaluation verification & exit tests

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed with the latency profile. As we discussed in the call, we want a concise finish-line checklist that spells out the acceptance tests we need to move from pilot -> production. High-level asks from our side:

- Clear success criteria (functional + perf)
- Explicit exit gates (what fails the eval)
- Minimal evidence required to sign off (artifacts we can hand to our SREs)
- A short MAP with owners and dates so procurement can map to PO timing

For context, our procurement deadline to include Redwood in the SOW is 2026-11-01. Can you send a one-pager / checklist and a short mutual action plan this week?

We'd like the evaluation to validate:
1) Response-time SDS: 95th pctile latency for 512-token queries under realistic concurrency
2) Cost per 1K tokens estimate for our workload (batching guidance welcome)
3) Privacy: no model-hosted logs outside our VPC + KMS integration
4) Functional accuracy: top-level instruction-following and hallucination tests on a 100-case probe set

Attaching our initial probe set (sent separately from QA).

Thanks,
Alyssa
Director, Platform Engineering
Clipper Health

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Green <alyssa@clipperhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Finish-line checklist: evaluation verification & exit tests

Alyssa — thanks for the clear asks and deadline. Attaching a recommended finish-line checklist (spreadsheet) and an evidence-template you can use to collect artifacts from the pilot. Quick summary / proposed MAP below — I kept it short so you can paste into procurement.

Proposed success criteria (must all be met for pass):
- Latency: 95th pctile <= 200ms for 512-token gen under target concurrency (TBD; propose 8 concurrent streams)
- Throughput: sustained >= 120 reqs/min per reserved instance profile
- Quality: probe-set concordance >= 0.92 (F1-style agreement on intent categories)
- Security/compliance: KMS key integration validated + SOC2 questionnaire responses uploaded
- Operational: end-to-end regression smoke run (50-case) with <= 2% failure rate

Exit gates (fail -> stop eval):
- Data exfiltration or storage outside agreed VPC patterns
- 95th pctile latency consistently > 350ms after two tuning cycles
- Quality regressions > 6 pts on the probe set vs baseline

Evidence we will supply (minimum):
- Latency histogram and sampling traces (artifact: latency-traces.json)
- Embedding similarity report and probe-set scoring (artifact: probe-results.csv)
- Config snapshot (model version, quantization profile)
- Signed SOC2 excerpt and KMS proof-of-setup

Proposed MAP (owner / target date):
- 10/09: 30-min alignment call — owners: Soojin (Redwood), Alyssa (Clipper) — outcome: lock probe set + concurrency profile
- 10/11: baseline smoke run & perf sweep (owner: Redwood SRE / Jonas) — outcome: perf report and tuning notes
- 10/14: security evidence package (owner: Karthik / Security) — outcome: SOC2 excerpt + KMS test logs
- 10/16: final verification run & handoff readiness review (owner: Customer Success / Soojin) — outcome: artifacts uploaded to shared Drive

I attached: finishline-checklist.xlsx (tabbed: criteria, tests, owners) and eval-evidence-template.md (fields for each artifact). Let me know if you'd like numbers tightened (e.g., lower latency target) — I can ask the runtime team for a targeted perf run.

Next steps: confirm 10/09 11:00am PT for a short alignment call and we'll circulate an invite.

Best,
Soojin
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: finishline-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), eval-evidence-template.md (markdown template)

From: Alyssa Green <alyssa@clipperhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, QA Team <qa@clipperhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T13:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Finish-line checklist: evaluation verification & exit tests

Thanks Soojin — this looks good and very close to what we need. Two asks from our side before the 10/09 call:

1) Can we tighten the perf SLAs slightly? If you can get 95th <= 180ms in the perf sweep that's ideal for our on-call SLOs. If not, we need to document fallback behaviors in the MAP.
2) Procurement asked for a short description of the evidence (one paragraph each) to drop into the SOW. Can you provide 1–2 sentence descriptions for the latency artifact, probe-set scoring, and KMS verification?

Also, our QA team will send the probe set and a small synthetic load script (attached). We'll expect Redwood to run the baseline sweep on 10/11 as proposed.

—Alyssa

On Oct 8, 2026, at 09:03 AM, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alyssa — thanks for the clear asks and deadline. Attaching a recommended finish-line checklist...

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Green <alyssa@clipperhealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-09T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Finish-line checklist: evaluation verification & exit tests

Alyssa — quick note from the deals/security side. We're aligned to the MAP and can hit the procurement timeline if the eval artifacts are delivered as planned. A few concrete commitments: 

- Deal ID: RDW-2026-1147 (use this in any SOW/PO references)
- Security: we'll provide KMS onboarding steps + test tokens; SOC2 excerpt will be uploaded to the Drive folder by 10/14
- Procurement: if Clipper confirms PO intent by 11/01 we can push reserved capacity hold for 11/08 (buffer for onboarding)

On technical specifics: Jonas will run the perf sweep (10/11) and capture both p50/p95 latencies, tail traces, and token-level cost estimates. For the quality gate we recommend a 0.92 similarity floor on embeddings and a pass rate >= 94% on the 50-case smoke run. If either threshold fails, we do one tuning cycle (params/quantization/profile) and re-run. If still failing, eval pauses.

I created a short HubSpot note under the deal with the MAP.

—Karthik

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Green <alyssa@clipperhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T18:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Finish-line checklist: evaluation verification & exit tests

Thanks all — summary and agreed actions below (locking in language you can paste into procurement / SOW).

Agreed finish-line criteria (final):
- Latency: 95th <= 180ms for 512-token queries at agreed concurrency (8 streams) — perf sweep on 10/11 (owner: Jonas)
- Throughput: sustained >= 120 reqs/min per instance profile after tuning (owner: Redwood SRE)
- Quality: probe-set concordance >= 0.92 on the master probe set (owner: Clipper + Redwood)
- Security: KMS integration verified + SOC2 excerpt uploaded by 10/14 (owner: Karthik)
- Smoke run: 50-case regression with <= 2% failures (owner: Redwood CS)

Exit gates (succinct):
- Evidence of data leaving agreed retention/VPC patterns
- Persistent latency above 350ms after one tuning cycle
- Quality drop > 6 pts vs baseline after tuning cycle

Deliverables and timeline (final MAP):
- 10/09 11:00 PT: Alignment call (locked) — invite sent
- 10/11: Perf baseline & sweep (Jonas) — deliverable: perf-report.zip
- 10/14: Security evidence upload (Karthik) — deliverable: soc2-excerpt.pdf + kms-test.log
- 10/16: Final verification run & artifacts (Soojin/CS) — deliverable: probe-results.csv, latency-traces.json
- 10/18: Final signoff window opens (Clipper) — target SOW inclusion by 11/01

Owners: Soojin (Redwood solutions lead), Jonas (Redwood SRE), Karthik (Deals/Security), Alyssa (Clipper platform lead)

Attachments: finishline-checklist.xlsx, eval-evidence-template.md. Drive folder and HubSpot link included above.

If everyone is aligned I'll push the MAP into the HubSpot deal and we can treat the 10/16 run as the last-blocking artifact before procurement.

Thanks — see you on the 10/09 call.

—Soojin
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
